For the selected family $R$, there exists a squarefree polynomial $A\in\mathbb{F}_{147457}[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree at most $23712$ such that $A_Z\ne0$ and $A(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ formally for every line $L\in R$.
lemmas.title: Weighted interpolation

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Every first-core line has at least $D+1=23713$ covered accepted points. At each such point $x$, the first-core line label and a selected alternative-line label both equal $f(x)$. The selected-line identity from P4 therefore gives $A(x,f(x))=0$.

For any first-core line $L$, the restriction $A(L(t),P_L(t))$ has degree at most $D=23712$ and has at least $D+1=23713$ distinct roots. It is therefore the zero polynomial.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, the formal identity $A(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ holds for every line vertex $L$ of the first core.
lemmas.title: First-core identity extension

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb{F}_{147457}[X,Y]$ is the greatest common divisor of the coefficients of $A$ as a polynomial in $Z$, and $B$ is primitive. Put
$$
h=\deg H,
\qquad
W=\operatorname{wdeg}(B),
\qquad
n=\deg_Z(B).
$$
The highest weighted-homogeneous parts multiply nontrivially, so
$$
h+W=\operatorname{wdeg}(A)\le D.
$$
The polynomial $B$ is squarefree and $B_Z\ne0$. Every irreducible factor of primitive $B$ has positive degree in $Z$. Since
$$
1\le n\le\left\lfloor\frac{D}{87}\right\rfloor=272<147457,
$$
every such factor has nonzero derivative with respect to $Z$, and hence
$$
\gcd(B,B_Z)=1.
$$
At most $h$ first-core lines divide $H$. On every other first-core line, cancellation in $\mathbb{F}_{147457}[t]$ gives
$$
B(L(t),P_L(t))=0.
$$
For $n\ge2$, the nonzero nominal discriminant $\Delta_Z(B)$ is homogeneous of coefficient degree $2n-2$ and coefficient-index weight $n(n-1)$. Consequently,
$$
\deg_{X,Y}\Delta_Z(B)\le(n-1)(2W-87n).
$$
If both $B(L(t),P_L(t))$ and $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ vanish formally, then $P_L$ is a repeated finite root over $\mathbb{F}_{147457}(t)$. Nominal-degree homogenization preserves this singular projective root even when the leading coefficient specializes to zero. Thus a defining linear form for $L$ divides the discriminant, without requiring inversion of the leading coefficient.

The combined number of content lines and derivative-degenerate lines is at most
$$
h+(n-1)(2W-87n)
\le
(n-1)(2D-87n)+(3-2n)h.
$$
For $n\ge2$, this is maximized at $h=0$. The successive difference is
$$
2(D-87(n-1))>0,
$$
so the maximum occurs at $n=272$ and equals
$$
271(47424-23664)=6438960.
$$
For $n=1$, a derivative-degenerate noncontent line would divide both coefficients of $B$, contradicting primitivity; only the at most $h\le D-87=23625$ content lines remain.

On every nonexceptional line, $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most
$$
W-87\le D-87=23625.
$$
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb{F}_{147457}[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content of $A$ in $Z$ and $B$ is primitive. There is a set of at most $6438960$ first-core lines such that every other first-core line $L$ satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ formally and has $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))\ne0$ of degree at most $23625$.
lemmas.title: Primitive discriminant cleanup

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Let the first core have $x$ points, $n$ lines, and $e\le6438960$ exceptional lines. Put
$$
a=22796,
\qquad
b=35928,
\qquad
B_0=aP+b\Lambda=1276874517475772.
$$
The actual first-peel loss is at most
$$
a(P-x)+b(\Lambda-n)=B_0-ax-bn.
$$
Inside the first core, removing exceptional-line edges and derivative-zero edges costs at most
$$
147457e+23625(n-e).
$$
After the exceptional lines are removed, peel point vertices of degree at most $D=23712$ and line vertices of degree at most $6046$. If this second peel empties the graph, it costs at most
$$
Dx+6046(n-e).
$$
Thus the total number of accepted edges is at most
$$
B_0-\mathcal{A}x-\mathcal{B}n+\mathcal{C}e,
$$
where
$$
\mathcal{A}=a-D=-916,
\qquad
\mathcal{B}=b-23625-6046=6257,
\qquad
\mathcal{C}=147457-23625-6046=117786.
$$
Because $\mathcal{A}<0$ and $\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C}>0$, use $x\le P$, the bound $n\ge3304806285$ from P2, and $e\le6438960$. The exact margin is
$$
(-916)P+6257\cdot3304806285-117786\cdot6438960
=
2646349001>0.
$$
An empty second core would therefore have at most
$$
B_0-2646349001=1276871871126771
$$
accepted edges. This is
$$
1276872883785185-1276871871126771=1012658414
$$
below the first-core threshold. Hence at least $1276872883785186$ accepted edges force a nonempty second core with the stated minimum degrees.

Every retained line inherits $B(L(t),P_L(t))=0$. At every retained point $x$, an accepted retained incidence gives $B(x,f(x))=0$, while the derivative cleanup gives $B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, every accepted incidence graph with at least $1276872883785186$ edges contains a nonempty subgraph $G_1$ of point minimum degree $23713$ and line minimum degree $6047$ such that every retained line $L$ satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ formally and every retained point $x$ satisfies $B(x,f(x))=0$ and $B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$.
lemmas.title: Amortized second-core survival

lemmas.proof_markdown:
For a connected component, let $a_c$, $b_c$, and $e_c$ be its point, line, and retained-edge densities. Put
$$
\alpha=\frac{23713}{p+1},
\qquad
\beta=\frac{6047}{p},
\qquad
c=\frac{\alpha}{\beta}=\frac{23713p}{6047(p+1)},
\qquad
\gamma^2=\frac{6047}{23713p}.
$$
The minimum-degree bounds and centered incidence mixing give
$$
e_c\ge\alpha a_c,
\qquad
e_c\ge\beta b_c,
$$
and
$$
e_c\le U_a(b_c):=a_cb_c+
\sqrt{\frac{a_c(1-a_c)b_c(1-b_c)}{p+1}}.
$$
At $b_0=ca_c$, if $a_c<\beta$ and $ca_c<1/2$, feasibility requires
$$
F(a_c):=(\beta-a_c)^2-\gamma^2(1-a_c)(1-ca_c)\le0.
$$
Indeed, $F(a_c)>0$ is equivalent to $U_a(b_0)<\alpha a_c=\beta b_0$. The function $U_a(b)$ is increasing for $b\le b_0<1/2$, while $U_a(b)/b$ decreases for $b\ge b_0$; the two ranges respectively contradict the two minimum-degree lower bounds.

Let
$$
\tau=\frac{638436441892593}{16031314402099210}.
$$
Exact arithmetic gives
$$
\beta-\tau=
\frac{18984760149317}{16031314402099210}>0,
$$
$$
\frac12-c\tau=
\frac{33331764458748924581}{96942015610695964780}>0,
$$
$$
F(\tau)=
\frac{7420334393983000788336097807}{6094354451541842980772389001448480200}>0,
$$
$$
F'(\tau)=
-\frac{224336802355813248}{95038284115116314405}<0,
$$
and
$$
F''=\frac{147457}{73729}>0.
$$
Since $F'$ is increasing, $F'(a)<0$ for every $0\le a\le\tau$. Hence $F(a)\ge F(\tau)>0$ throughout this interval, contradicting feasibility. Thus every component has point density strictly greater than $\tau$.

Moreover,
$$
\tau P=
\frac{638436441892593}{737290}
=
865923099+
\frac{230883}{737290}.
$$
Every component therefore contains at least $865923100$ points.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, every connected component of the simple-root core has point density strictly greater than $638436441892593/16031314402099210$.
lemmas.title: Component point mass

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Choose a point $b$ in a connected component of the simple-root core. It has at least $D+1=23713>D$ retained incident lines. Their labels have degree at most $87$, share the value $f(b)$, satisfy the formal identities for $B$, and have the common simple root certified by $B_Z(b,f(b))\ne0$.

KTZ Lemmas 2.7 and 6.1 produce a polynomial $Q$ of total degree at most $87$ such that
$$
B(X,Y,Q)=0
$$
and $Q$ agrees with every seed-line label.

Suppose propagation has reached a retained line $L$ and an accepted point $x\in L$. Then
$$
Q(x)=P_L(x)=f(x).
$$
On any adjacent retained line $M$, both $Q|_M$ and $P_M$ are degree-at-most-$87$ roots of the same formal equation and have the same simple value at $x$. The one-variable uniqueness argument from KTZ Lemma 2.7 makes the two restrictions identical. Connectivity propagates the same $Q$ throughout the component. Hence $Q(x)=f(x)$ at every point vertex of the component, which is the invariant-based propagation of KTZ Lemma 6.3.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, every connected component of the simple-root core has a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_{147457}[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $87$ such that $Q(x)=f(x)$ for every point vertex $x$ in the component.
lemmas.title: Formal reconstruction

lemmas.proof_markdown:
There are
$$
N=p^2(p+1)=3206262880419842
$$
uniform point-line incidences. The threshold is
$$
\epsilon=
\frac{1276872883785185+1}{N}
=
\frac{638436441892593}{1603131440209921}.
$$
Acceptance at least $\epsilon$ supplies at least $1276872883785186$ accepted edges. By P7, a nonempty simple-root core survives. By P8 and P9, one polynomial $Q$ of total degree at most $87$ agrees with $f$ on strictly more than
$$
\frac{\epsilon}{10}
=
\frac{638436441892593}{16031314402099210}
$$
of the plane, and hence on at least one tenth of the stated threshold.

The current verified record is
$$
\frac{5759100500000001}{10^{16}}.
$$
The comparison is exact:
$$
5759100500000001\cdot1603131440209921
-
10^{16}\cdot638436441892593
=
2848230659952747739191940209921>0.
$$
Thus the fixed-instance threshold is strictly below that record.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, let $f:\mathbb{F}_{147457}^{2}\to\mathbb{F}_{147457}$ be a point table, and assign a polynomial of degree at most $87$ to every affine line. If uniform affine-line-then-point acceptance is at least $638436441892593/1603131440209921$, then there exists $Q\in\mathbb{F}_{147457}[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $87$ whose agreement with $f$ is at least $638436441892593/16031314402099210$.
lemmas.title: Soundness conclusion

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Take
$$
B=Z^{147457}-X.
$$
This polynomial is squarefree because $B_X=-1$. In characteristic $147457$,
$$
B_Z=147457Z^{147456}=0.
$$
Its degree in $Z$ is $147457$, whereas the reconstruction proof has the strict bound
$$
\deg_Z(B)\le272<147457.
$$
That bound excludes this inseparable example.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, there exists a squarefree polynomial $B\in\mathbb{F}_{147457}[X,Y,Z]$ such that $B_Z=0$.
lemmas.title: Inseparability example

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Take
$$
A=X(Z-Y).
$$
Viewed as a polynomial in $Z$, all its coefficients are divisible by $X$. On the affine line $X=0$, parameterized by $L(t)=(0,t)$, every line label $P_L$ satisfies
$$
A(L(t),P_L(t))=A(0,t,P_L(t))=0.
$$
Thus the content factor makes the trivariate identity independent of the line label.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, there exist $A\in\mathbb{F}_{147457}[X,Y,Z]$ and an affine line $L$ such that a defining linear form for $L$ divides the coefficient content of $A$ in $Z$ and $A(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ for every degree-at-most-$87$ line polynomial $P_L$.
lemmas.title: Coefficient-content example

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Take
$$
B=Z^2-X
$$
and use the zero label on the line $X=0$. Then both
$$
B(0,t,0)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
B_Z(0,t,0)=0
$$
hold formally. The discriminant is
$$
\Delta_Z(B)=4X,
$$
so the bad line occurs with multiplicity exactly one. Hence discriminant multiplicity alone cannot yield a smaller uniform line charge.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, there exist a polynomial $B$, an affine line $L$, and a degree-at-most-$87$ label $P_L$ such that $B(L(t),P_L(t))=B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ formally while a defining linear form for $L$ occurs with multiplicity one in $\Delta_Z(B)$.
lemmas.title: Discriminant multiplicity

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Take
$$
B=XZ^3+(Z-Y)^2.
$$
Specializing to the line $X=0$ removes the cubic leading term and leaves
$$
B(0,Y,Z)=(Z-Y)^2.
$$
The finite root $Z=Y$ remains repeated. Thus nominal-degree homogenization retains the relevant singular root even when specialization lowers the leading degree.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, there exists a polynomial $B\in\mathbb{F}_{147457}[X,Y,Z]$ whose leading coefficient in $Z$ vanishes upon specialization to an affine line while the specialized polynomial retains a repeated finite root.
lemmas.title: Leading-coefficient specialization

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Choose a product $g(X)$ of $23625$ distinct linear factors and set
$$
B=Z(Z+g(X)).
$$
The polynomial $B$ is primitive and squarefree. With weights $1,1,87$,
$$
\operatorname{wdeg}(B)=23625+87=23712.
$$
On the line $Y=0$ with zero label,
$$
B_Z(X,0,0)=g(X),
$$
which is nonzero and has exactly $23625$ distinct roots. Thus the derivative-root budget of $23625$ is attained.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, there exists a primitive squarefree polynomial $B$ of weighted degree $23712$ and a nonexceptional affine line with a degree-at-most-$87$ label on which the derivative restriction has exactly $23625$ distinct zeros.
lemmas.title: Derivative-root budget

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_{23712}$ be distinct affine line forms vanishing at a common point and set
$$
B=Z-\prod_{i=1}^{23712}\ell_i.
$$
On each line $\ell_i=0$, the zero label is a root, and
$$
B_Z=1,
$$
so the common value is simple. Since $B$ is linear in $Z$, every global polynomial root must be
$$
Q=\prod_{i=1}^{23712}\ell_i,
$$
which has total degree $23712>87$. Hence $23712$ seed lines do not force a global root of total degree at most $87$.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_{23712}$ be distinct affine line forms through one point and let $B=Z-\prod_{i=1}^{23712}\ell_i$. The zero labels on the lines $\ell_i=0$ are simple roots of $B$, while every global polynomial root of $B$ has total degree $23712>87$.
lemmas.title: Seed-line barrier

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Take
$$
B=Z^2-XY.
$$
For every $c\in\mathbb{F}_{147457}$, the line $Y=c^2X$ through the origin carries the degree-one roots $Z=cX$ and $Z=-cX$. A global polynomial root would satisfy
$$
Q^2=XY,
$$
which is impossible in the unique factorization domain $\mathbb{F}_{147457}[X,Y]$ because the multiplicities of $X$ and $Y$ on the right-hand side are odd. At the common branch point,
$$
B_Z(0,0,0)=0.
$$
Thus the local branches intersect singularly and do not determine a polynomial global branch.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, the relation $B=Z^2-XY$ has concurrent degree-one line roots but no polynomial global root, and their common branch point satisfies $B_Z=0$.
lemmas.title: Singular branch barrier

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Set $f=0$. Give every line in $58829$ directions the constant label $0$, and give every line in every other direction the constant label $1$. Every incidence on a zero-labelled line is accepted, and no incidence on a one-labelled line is accepted. Hence the acceptance probability is
$$
\frac{58829}{p+1}=
\frac{58829}{147458}.
$$
With $P=p^2=21743566849$ and $B_{\mathrm{geom}}=1276872883785185$,
$$
58829P-(B_{\mathrm{geom}}+1)=18062022413>0.
$$
Therefore this acceptance is strictly above
$$
\frac{B_{\mathrm{geom}}+1}{p^2(p+1)}
=
\frac{638436441892593}{1603131440209921}.
$$
The constant polynomial $Q=0$ agrees with $f$ everywhere.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, there is a point table and a degree-at-most-$87$ affine-line table whose acceptance is concentrated entirely in $58829$ directions and is strictly greater than $638436441892593/1603131440209921$.
lemmas.title: Concentrated directions

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Choose $f:\mathbb{F}_p^2\to\mathbb{F}_p$ uniformly at random. For a fixed polynomial $Q$ of total degree at most $87$, its number of agreements with $f$ is binomial with mean $p$. There are $p^{3916}$ such formal polynomials because
$$
\binom{87+2}{2}=3916.
$$
A Chernoff bound followed by a union bound over these polynomials shows that some point table $f$ has fewer than $2p$ agreements with every such $Q$.

On each affine line, interpolate the values of this $f$ at $88$ points. The resulting line polynomial has degree at most $87$ and supplies at least $88$ accepted incidences on that line. Thus the line table has acceptance at least
$$
\frac{88}{p}.
$$
For every
$$
\epsilon\in\left[\frac{20}{p},\frac{88}{p}\right],
$$
the acceptance is at least $\epsilon$, whereas every polynomial $Q$ has agreement strictly less than
$$
\frac{2}{p}\le\frac{\epsilon}{10}.
$$
The soundness implication therefore fails throughout the stated interval.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, there exist a point table and a degree-at-most-$87$ affine-line table with acceptance at least $88/147457$ such that every polynomial of total degree at most $87$ agrees with the point table on fewer than $2\cdot147457$ points; consequently, soundness fails for every $\epsilon\in[20/147457,88/147457]$.
lemmas.title: Adversarial score interval

lemmas.proof_markdown:
A point table on $p^2$ points takes only $p$ values. By the pigeonhole principle, some value occurs at least $p$ times. The constant polynomial with that value therefore has agreement at least
$$
\frac{p}{p^2}=
\frac1p.
$$
Whenever $\epsilon\le10/p$, this agreement is at least $\epsilon/10$, independently of the acceptance probability.
lemmas.statement_markdown: In the fixed instance $m=2$, $p=147457$, and $d=87$, every point table agrees with a constant polynomial on at least a $1/147457$ fraction of the plane; hence for every $\epsilon\le10/147457$, the agreement conclusion at level $\epsilon/10$ holds independently of acceptance.
lemmas.title: Constant-polynomial floor

nodes.notes: No probabilistic or rounding loss occurs here. The aligned score $A_\star$ is $1187$ points below the comparison threshold $7810920777$. Primality and the displayed counts require fresh active-corpus discharge.

For the accepted-incidence set $E$, let $\operatorname{Pass}=|E|/N$. Set $$A_\star=7810919590,\qquad \varepsilon_\star=\frac{A_\star}{M},\qquad \tau_\star=\frac{\varepsilon_\star}{10}=\frac{781091959}{M},$$ $$k_\star=A_\star P_0=1151782580902220.$$ Then $\operatorname{Pass}\ge\varepsilon_\star$ iff $|E|\ge k_\star$, and $\lceil\varepsilon_\star M\rceil=A_\star$.

nodes.notes: This replaces hard popularity pruning by the additive missed-incidence loss $\Delta_\star\approx0.0831401$. It is the sharp point-degree-only interface used by the candidate ledger, but must be reproved because the active evidence index is empty.
nodes.statement_markdown: Put $D=17642$, $r=600782$, and $j=51837$. For $0\le a\le P_0$, let $$H_a=\frac{\binom{\Lambda-a}{r}}{\binom{\Lambda}{r}},\qquad \phi_a=aH_a.$$ One has $$\phi_a\le\frac{(P_0-a)\phi_j+(a-j)\phi_{P_0}}{P_0-j},$$ $$H_j<\frac{238762637131533}{10^{15}},\qquad H_{P_0}<\frac{17003158362223}{10^{15}}.$$ If $|E|/N\ge\varepsilon_\star$, there is an $r$-line set $R$ such that the number $U_R$ of accepted incidences at points whose accepted pencils miss $R$ satisfies $$\frac{U_R}{N}<\Delta_\star:=\frac{1728600563034852992358241217}{20791416056682290000000000000}.$$

nodes.label: Lossless squarefree weighted interpolation
nodes.notes: Interpolation deletes no accepted incidence. The choice $D=17642$ balances the later $D$-point charge against the energy loss and leaves exactly $1281$ dimensions of surplus.
nodes.statement_markdown: With weights $(1,1,87)$, $$V_D=\sum_{z=0}^{202}\binom{D-87z+2}{2}=10599598107>r(D+1)=10599596826.$$ For every $r$-line set $R$, there is a nonzero squarefree $\mathscr A\in F[X,Y,Z]$ such that $$\operatorname{wdeg}(\mathscr A)\le D,\qquad \deg_Z\mathscr A\le202<p,\qquad \mathscr A_Z\ne0,$$ and $\mathscr A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$ for every $L\in R$.

nodes.label: Mass-preserving identity-line extension
nodes.notes: This transfers the interpolant without a second popularity threshold. Its only loss is at most $D$ accepted hit incidences on each line not transferred to $T$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Call an accepted point on $L\notin R$ hit if its accepted pencil meets $R$, and let $$T=R\cup\{L\notin R:L\text{ contains more than }D\text{ hit accepted points}\}.$$ Every $L\in T$ satisfies $\mathscr A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$. If $t=|T|$ and $E_T$ is the accepted edge set on $T$, then $$|E|\le |E_T|+U_R+D(\Lambda-t).$$

nodes.label: Primitive factorization and discriminant cleanup
nodes.notes: This bounds the factorization losses by $p$ edges on each of at most $3559710$ exceptional lines and by at most $q=17555$ derivative-zero points on every other identity line. Nominal-degree homogenization is required to handle leading-coefficient collapse.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $\mathscr A=CB$, where $C\in F[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content and $B$ is primitive in $Z$. Then $B$ is squarefree, $1\le\deg_ZB\le202<p$, and $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. Among the lines of $T$, at most $$E_D=3559710$$ are content lines or satisfy $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$. Every other $L\in T$ satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ is nonzero of degree at most $$q=D-87=17555.$$

\qquad K=2D(s-1)-Z=193111783.$$

Suppose $D+1$ distinct affine lines through $x_0$ carry degree-at-most-$87$ formal roots $P_L$ of $B$ satisfying $$P_L(x_0)=a,\\ B_Z(x_0,a)\ne0.$$ Then there exists $Q\in F[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $87$ such that $B(X,Y,Q(X,Y))=0$ and $Q|_L=P_L$ on every seed line.

nodes.label: Exact unconditional soundness interval
nodes.notes: The recovery loss is exactly the required factor $10$: $1/p\ge\varepsilon/10$. This discontinuously lowers the available trigger from the configured comparison value to every positive rational at most $10/p$.

nodes.notes: Exact ceiling arithmetic reduces the comparison count from $7810920777$ to $1$, a gain of $7810920776$ points. Positivity proves that no further absolute-count improvement is possible.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $$\varepsilon_*=10^{-11},\qquad \bar\varepsilon=\frac1M=\frac1{21743566849}.$$ Then $$\varepsilon_*\le\bar\varepsilon\le\frac{10}{147457},$$ $$\left\lceil N\varepsilon_*\right\rceil=32063,\qquad A_*:=\left\lceil M\varepsilon_*\right\rceil=1,$$ and $$\left\lceil\frac{M\varepsilon_*}{10}\right\rceil=\left\lceil\frac{A_*}{10}\right\rceil=1.$$ For the configured comparison value $\varepsilon_0=359229046020947/10^{15}$, $$A_0:=\left\lceil M\varepsilon_0\right\rceil=7810920777>A_*.$$ For every real $\delta>0$, $$\lceil M\delta\rceil\ge1.$$
